gen-dafont-ethnocentric-inter: Ethnocentric stretches its letters wide apart, with short ascenders perched above big round bowls, and it looks like it is already moving. Inter sits beneath it as a smooth, tube-like line of sans, and if the heading shrinks, that speed gets lost.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-mulish: Fast and pushy, Ethnocentric spaces its letters far apart over big bowls and low-slung ascenders. Mulish steps in with a plain sans cut of one uniform depth, soft horseshoe openings, and a large x-height that makes the pair feel approachable.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab carries a precise, structured texture where the middle zone of the lowercase does most of the work. Ethnocentric above it is all spaced-out speed, so the slab-serif lines read as the steady ground under a fast-moving headline.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-esteban: Industrial and modern up top, Existence is drawn like thread stitched along a path. Esteban follows with a text serif whose thin parts barely slim down, so the page moves from stitched wire to a refined, classic voice.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-faustina: Faustina reads as classic and authoritative, its bowls thinning gently and its c opening like a pair of pliers. Existence glows above it like a neon tube of one steady thickness, while the serif underneath keeps a softer thick-thin rhythm.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-halant: Industrial lettering leads here, with Existence drawn in pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin. And Halant answers with a faint tug of heavier verticals, a towering x-height, and outward-pointing terminals that feel traditional and sure of themselves.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-hedvig-letters-s: Hedvig Letters Serif reads with authority, its open-ended curves and sturdy lowercase body giving each line a classic footing. Existence sits above it with no calligraphic thinning at all, while the serif's joins and terminals turn just slightly lighter.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-marcellus-sc: Marcellus SC brings dignified, literary stature, with mild stroke contrast and terminals pulled well back. Existence is the one to lean on for a marker-like constant line and industrial punch, while Marcellus SC is better at the quiet, serif-led reading.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-montagu-slab: Existence has no hairlines to squint at, just constant strokes and wide, porthole-like counters that hold up even when small. Montagu Slab then reads comfortably, with sturdy bowls, a sizable x-height and lightly thinned links in its g.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-henta: Noto Serif Hentaigana reads in a refined, traditional way, with open jaws on its curves and the mild variation of a dip pen used gently. Its pull against Existence, drawn like thin plastic tubing, is the pair's strongest quality.
